title: Long Life and Old Age
lead: From the long lives of Genesis 5 to the seventy or eighty years of Psalm 90:10, the Bible treats long life as a blessing and its shortening as a mark of a fallen world, and the prophets promise a renewal in which no one dies young (Isaiah 65:20).

sections.b: Genesis gives the first fathers lives of centuries (Genesis 5) and then has the LORD say, "Their days will be 120 years" (Genesis 6:3), which some read as a limit on the length of a life and others as the time left before the Flood; after the Flood the ages fall (Genesis 11). The law promises long life on the land to those who honor their parents (Exodus 20:12). Psalm 90:10 sets the span at seventy, or eighty for the strong. Old age is honored, and "gray hair is a crown of beauty" (Proverbs 16:31). Isaiah 65:20-22 promises a new creation where whoever dies at a hundred dies young, and the lifetime of God's people is like that of a tree.
sections.refs: Genesis 5:1-32; Genesis 6:3; Genesis 11:10-32; Exodus 20:12; Psalm 90:10; Isaiah 65:20-22; Proverbs 16:31
